subject: science
confirmedFrom: Front matter (General Marking Instructions: Introduction, Assessment objectives, Quality of candidates' responses, Flexibility in marking, Positive marking, Awarding zero marks, Marking Calculations, Types of mark schemes, Levels of response, Quality of written communication) of the Summer 2025 P1 Higher mark scheme, docs/sources/papers/science/2025-Summer/P1-H-Physics-MS-67250.txt, read 2026-09-05, plus the Physics 'Subject-specific Instructions' (Summer 2019 / Summer 2021 P2 schemes) and the Biology 'Symbols and terms' table (Summer 2021 B1/B2 schemes). Notation counted over all 242 Standard science mark schemes 2018-2026 under docs/sources/papers/science.
legal: Rules rewritten in our own words; only notation tokens, abbreviations and band labels are reproduced verbatim. No answer content is stored.
notation: CCEA science schemes use no letter codes. Each marking point is a line ending in [1] (9849 occurrences), part totals appear as [n] in the margin, and a running 'AVAILABLE MARKS' column totals each question (497). We label a marking point 'P' internally and a 6-mark banded question 'QWC'.

codes.label: marking point
codes.meaning: One creditworthy piece of information, worth [1] (occasionally [2]); a part's mark is the number of points hit, up to the cap in the margin. Points may be independent, or dependent on an earlier point ('dep' / '(threshold)').
codes.source: CCEA Double Award Science mark-scheme layout, Summer 2025 P1 H MS; 'Types of mark schemes' (point-for-point marking); counts from the 242-scheme corpus scan 2026-09-05

codes.label: quality of written communication (banded)
codes.meaning: The one 6-mark extended-writing question per paper, marked by counting indicative-content points to place the answer in Band A [5]-[6], Band B [3]-[4] or Band C [1]-[2] (D = [0], response not worthy of credit), then placing it within the band on the quality of communication.
codes.source: CCEA Double Award Science MS 'Levels of response' and 'Quality of written communication', Summer 2025 P1 H MS pp.2-3; specification §4.4; counts from the corpus scan 2026-09-05; bands in packs/science/exam-true/qwc-bands.json

conventions.meaning: the point that must be present before the other marks in that part can be given (e.g. the definition's core idea before its qualifier). Our reading of scheme usage; the front matter defines 'threshold performance' only for banded answers.
conventions.source: Summer 2025 P1 H MS Q1(a), Q4(b); Summer 2025 U7 Physics Booklet B MS Q4(b); corpus scan

conventions.meaning: error carried forward: a wrong earlier number used correctly later still earns the later marks
conventions.source: Physics Subject-specific Instructions (Summer 2019 P2 MS); Biology symbols table (Summer 2021 B1 MS: E.C.F.); 'Marking Calculations' section of every scheme

conventions.meaning: this mark depends on the previous point being correct
one mark for each correct item in a list or table

conventions.token: Any two from / any three from
conventions.meaning: credit up to the stated number of the listed points; extra wrong items may invoke the listing rule
conventions.source: corpus scan 2026-09-05 (any two from 152, any three from 63, any one from 20, any four from 11)

conventions.meaning: an extra mark awarded within the same line of working (e.g. substitution + evaluation)
separates acceptable alternatives for the same point (only one mark between them)
conventions.source: Biology symbols table, Summer 2021 B1 MS

conventions.meaning: bracketed text is not required for the mark; it gives context (units in brackets are not demanded)
conventions.source: Biology symbols table, Summer 2021 B1 MS; '(J)', '(s)' in Summer 2025 P1 H MS

conventions.meaning: bold text in the scheme is essential for the mark
conventions.source: Biology symbols table, Summer 2021 B1 MS

conventions.token: Not / Not allow / Do not accept / Reject
conventions.meaning: a wording that must not be credited
conventions.source: corpus scan (NOT 33, Not 28, not accept 21, do not allow 6, do not accept 2)

conventions.meaning: a marker note about a common response
the unit is part of the answer mark
NOT used by CCEA Double Award Science schemes (0 occurrences); do not use in our schemes

rules.text: Schemes indicate the range of creditworthy responses; examiners use professional judgement for unanticipated valid answers and refer difficult cases upwards.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Introduction, Flexibility in marking), Summer 2025 P1 H MS

rules.text: Credit what the candidate knows and can do rather than penalising omissions — except in complex calculations, which are marked by error or omission.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Positive marking), Summer 2025 P1 H MS

rules.text: Where one response is required, a correct answer written alongside a wrong one earns nothing (the listing rule). Contradictory ticks cancel.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Positive marking, last paragraph), Summer 2025 P1 H MS; research 03 §7.1

rules.text: No marks for an answer that is completely wrong or irrelevant.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Awarding zero marks), Summer 2025 P1 H MS

rules.text: In calculations a slip is penalised once; later steps and conclusions drawn correctly from the wrong number still earn their marks (ecf).
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Marking Calculations), Summer 2025 P1 H MS

rules.text: Short-answer questions are marked point for point; extended-writing questions are marked in bands that include the quality of written communication.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Types of mark schemes), Summer 2025 P1 H MS

rules.text: For banded answers the examiner counts the indicative-content points present to choose the band, then uses the quality of communication to place the mark within the band: a just-qualifying answer sits at the bottom of the range, a fully satisfying one at the top.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Levels of response), Summer 2025 P1 H MS

rules.text: The standard expected is that of a good 16-year-old; full marks are available for a response as good as can reasonably be expected at that age.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Quality of candidates' responses; Positive marking), Summer 2025 P1 H MS

rules.text: In numerical physics questions a correct answer with unit from a valid starting point gets full credit even if intermediate steps are missing; intermediate quantities need no units. This does not apply to proofs and derivations, which must be valid at every stage.
rules.source: CCEA Physics Subject-specific Instructions, Summer 2019 P2 MS (docs/sources/papers/science/2019-Summer/P2-H-Physics-MS-10000.txt); also Summer 2021 P2 schemes

rules.text: No credit for substituting numbers into a physically wrong equation or for the arithmetic that follows it; a wrong equation with a right number scores nothing. Later steps that use an earlier wrong number in a correct equation earn full credit (ecf).
rules.source: CCEA Physics Subject-specific Instructions, Summer 2019 P2 MS; CER March 2026 (research 03 §2)

rules.text: An arithmetic or unit slip normally loses only the answer/unit mark; a substitution error loses the substitution and answer marks; a power-of-ten slip counts as arithmetic and loses the answer mark only.
rules.source: CCEA Physics Subject-specific Instructions, Summer 2019 P2 MS

rules.text: Write the equation in symbols or words before substituting; the equation line is usually its own mark and is the entry ticket to the rest.
rules.source: Summer 2025 P1 H MS Q4(a), Q4(c) ([1] for the equation, [1] substitution, [1] answer, [1] unit); research 03 §7.1

rules.text: Wrong spelling is not penalised if the word is recognisable and is not another similar term; near-identical pairs (ureter/urethra) must be exactly right.
rules.source: CCEA Biology mark scheme 'Spelling' note, Summer 2021 B1 F MS (docs/sources/papers/science/2021-Summer/B1-F-Biology-MS-18437.txt)

rules.text: Chemical symbols are case-sensitive (Cu, not CU); ions are named as ions ('chloride ion', not 'chlorine ion'); observations must be fully qualified ('colourless solution', 'heat given out'); numerical answers to the stated decimal places.
rules.source: research 03 §7.1 (Chief Examiner reports, all series)

rules.text: Balanced equations are marked as reactants [1], products [1], balancing [1] (three points) for symbol/ionic equations; state symbols only when asked.
rules.source: Summer 2025 C1 H MS Q1(d)(i) (docs/sources/papers/science/2025-Summer/C1-H-Chemistry-MS-67236.txt)

rules.text: Ar and Mr values come from the Data Leaflet's Periodic Table; a wrong Ar loses the Mr mark but later steps follow through.
rules.source: research 03 §2 (Data Leaflet provided in C1, C2, Unit 7 Chemistry A and B); sci.ms.carry-error-through

rules.text: Definitions are marked against the key words of the CCEA glossaries; missing key words ('about a point', 'in equilibrium', 'weight acts') lose the mark.
rules.source: research 03 §7.1, §7.4 (Unit 7 Physics Booklet B Summer 2025)

rules.text: Convert to base units before substituting (g → kg, cm → m, minutes → s, mA → A); the unit on the answer line is often a separate mark.
rules.source: Summer 2025 P1 H MS Q1(b)(ii) (unit mark); research 03 §7.1, §7.4

rules.text: Comparisons need comparative language about both things being compared, with values where data is given.
rules.source: research 03 §7.1

rules.text: Black ink, HB pencil for drawings and graphs, answers inside the box, capital letters and full stops in QWC answers, cross out unwanted attempts.
rules.source: Paper front-page instructions (Summer 2025 P1 H, C1 H, U7 Physics Booklet B); research 03 §7.1

feedbackTemplates.P0-reject: Not credited: '{given}' is on the scheme's reject list — the examiner wants '{required}'.
feedbackTemplates.listing: You listed '{correct}' alongside '{incorrect}'. CCEA gives nothing for a correct answer next to a wrong one — one answer only.
feedbackTemplates.threshold: The threshold point ({threshold}) is missing, so the follow-on marks in this part cannot be given.
feedbackTemplates.ecf: Error carried forward: your value {value} is wrong, but you used it correctly, so this step still earns its mark.
feedbackTemplates.equation-first: Write the equation before the numbers: {equation}. The equation line is a mark on its own, and a wrong equation with a right number scores nothing.
feedbackTemplates.unit: Answer mark earned; the unit mark is lost — the answer needs {unit}.
feedbackTemplates.qwc-band: Band {band} ({range}): {pointsHit} of {pointsListed} indicative points, {quality}. To reach Band {next}: {upgrade}.
